newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian currency and gold reserves are $16 billion.
newsitem.headline: Russian currency and gold reserves are $16 billion.

text.p: The Russian Central Bank's gross foreign exchange and gold reserves are currently about $16 billion, a senior bank official said on Tuesday.
M2 money supply was running at 280-285 trillion roubles, including a monetary base of 126-127 trillion roubles, First Deputy Chairman Sergei Aleksashenko told a news conference.

"We consider this level of gold and currency reserves higher than the minimum necessary (to defend the rouble rate against the dollar)," Aleksashenko said. "But nevertheless we would like to raise this level of reserves, raise both its components."
It would only be possible to increase reserves if the rouble became more attractive, he said.
Earlier the central bank announced a continuation of its rouble policy throughout 1997, allowing for a gentle depreciation of the rouble by setting daily upper and lower limits against the dollar.
The rate of decline of the rouble is slower than in 1996.
Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin previously said reserves on July 15 were $14.9 billion.
According to central bank figures, reserves were $17.2 billion on January 1.
M2 money supply was 277.3 trillion roubles on October 1, and 220.8 trillion on January 1.
